facts.text: Cedars is an unincorporated community in Worcester Township, Montgomery County, Pennsylvania, located at the intersection of PA Route 73 and Bustard Road.
Formerly called Cedar Hills, Cedars is one of three historic villages in Worcester Township, reflecting the area's rural roots since 1733.
The village sits within the Skippack Creek watershed, a tributary of the Perkiomen Creek, supporting wetlands for amphibians and migratory birds.
Though never a battlefield, Cedars’ proximity to Valley Forge meant residents likely supplied the Continental Army during Washington’s 1777‑78 winter encampment.
In the mid‑1800s, turnpikes like Skippack Pike and the Reading Railroad’s Perkiomen Branch linked Cedars to Philadelphia, boosting local produce trade.
The area’s climate is humid continental, with hot summers averaging 84°F and snowy winters averaging 25 inches of snow annually.
